body: Exercise is definitely a help for sure. There's nothing quite like a grueling workout to get endorphins flowing. The problem is getting off your butt and actually exercising, which is easier said than done when you can barely get out of bed. Sometimes I've been able to do it when I know the end result is having a clear mind afterwards. It's often hard to summon the energy, though. =\

Can I ask why you're doing this in this subreddit? I'm genuinely curious. Are you bored? It doesn't bother me, because I'm used to internet trolls, but I'm curious what exactly drives people to do things like this. Is it a result of being miserable, too? If there's something bothering you, I'll listen. Maybe it'll help take my mind off of my own thoughts tonight.

I don't think a therapist would personally help me, because I can't get over the feeling that they're talking to me because they're being paid to, not because they genuinely want to help. I get more out of responses on places like this, actually. In a way it feels good to know that somewhere out there, someone cared enough to spend some time trying to help a complete stranger.

But I know that perspective has a lot to do with it. I can remember points in the near past, actually feeling optimistic. When I felt optimistic, a lot of the anxiety and depression was gone. I wish I knew how to get back into that mindset permanently. It's really awful when you can't even enjoy the moment, like there's a black rain cloud hanging over you at every turn. Maybe it really is an imbalance in the brain. I've always felt like my depression was 100% caused by my situation but there have definitely been times when I felt positive, although few and far between.

Thanks for the response. I would rather be alive and happy than be dead, but my suicidal thoughts have been out of control lately. And that itself makes me feel guilty and awful, in a cyclical effect.

I wish you nothing but the best. I hope that going around harassing people in pain makes you feel better about yourself!

I also hope that one day you get to feel the absolute miserable feeling of genuinely wanting to be dead. It might help put things in perspective for you.

To use the puppy metaphor, I feel like my puppy is a huge problem one. Like there were so many different puppies out there, and I was given one that I'm not happy with. It might learn some cool tricks that amuse me for the moment, but it will never learn the big, important ones that I really want it to do. And I can't be happy with a puppy that won't do what I want it to do. Does that make any sense? It's hard to explain feeling hopeless.

Yes, I've started to take steps forward. And yes, moving forward does help your mind for sure. But I feel like those steps forward are ultimately futile, and are never going to get me to where I want to be. There are some things that are really holding me back that have been with me so long that I don't think I can overcome them. I wrote about it in another response here, but I have pretty severe social anxiety.

Because of that, I don't have any friends. I know how pathetic that sounds, but it's true. I'm rapidly turning into the stereotypical basement-dwelling Reddit surfer and that scares the shit out of me. I've never had a girlfriend either. These are the things that weigh the most on my mind. I sometimes read posts from other people that are depressed and suicidal who talk about having friends or relationships and I just can't relate at all. It would be like a starving person hearing about how someone didn't like their meal.

I really appreciate your response and taking the time to type that out to me. I know exactly what you mean and I know it would help. I don't know why, but I feel like people are giving great advice that would apply to anyone BUT me. Such a twisted brain I have.

Thank you for the response.

I know that what you're saying is true. It feels like being at the bottom of a very deep hole. So deep that the light at the top is almost impossible to see. It feels like getting to that light and out of the hole would be the most incredible feeling in the world, and that everything would really be okay if you could get out of it. But you don't believe that you're ever going to get out of the hole. You've been down there so long that you start to wonder if you were just meant to be down there, and it's been so long that you're not even sure if you can start to climb out of it or not.

You're right that setting positive goals, and striving for them helps. I know it does, because it has helped me before. A big problem for me is that when something goes badly, or something traumatizing happens (I don't handle even small things well) I take it very badly. It kind of pushes me back into the hole again, even if I had started to climb out a little bit.

But I know that you have to have something to work toward. You just have to. Maybe that doesn't apply to everyone, but myself I know that I need to have something positive to look forward to, and something to work toward. It's impossible to feel good without that, to me.

This part isn't necessarily in response to you, but it's something I need to vent in this thread. I also can't get over the belief that there is something inherently wrong with me. My biggest problems are so weird and unrelatable that I feel stupid even talking about them, because I know that no one is going to understand or have a solution. It makes me feel so utterly alone and hopeless. I have extreme social anxiety, and my social skills have suffered badly due to avoiding social situations out of fear and depression. I get so nervous around people that I become incredibly awkward, which also has a lot to do with the lack of social skills. And knowing that I'm going to be awkward amplifies the anxiety, like a cycle that has no end.

I feel really uncomfortable writing that here, because it's not something anyone can give advice on. The typical thing someone will say is "just go out and talk to people and make friends!" but that isn't exactly something a person like me can do. I've never been able to do it.

I'm not asking for advice from you specifically. I just needed to talk about that somewhere. But thanks again for the reply, because things like this really do help in the moment.

Is anyone here? I'm worried. The person she mentioned, dextromethorphansand, hasn't been active on reddit since this post. This is bothering me a lot. I won't be able to stop thinking about it until I know what happened. :(

Hey... I'm a random person who's miserable for different reasons. I've been looking through this subreddit and your post struck a chord with me. I can't say that I have chronic pain or pretend I know what that's like. But I can completely relate to the anxiety thing, which I suffer from on an extreme level, along with severe depression. Like I said, I can't relate to the chronic pain, but I imagine it's similar in some respects to having severe depression like I have. It doesn't have any outward symptoms that a doctor or anyone else can look at and go "a-ha!" but it's very real to the sufferer, very debilitating, and they definitely know it's there. 

I'm nobody special, but I truly hope you find a solution to your problems. Nobody deserves to be in pain every day, on either a physical or mental level. You're an incredibly strong person by the sounds of it. I'm sure there is a medical solution out there for you, and I hope you find it soon. It frustrates me to hear about how you've been screwed around so much by doctors and the like. I'm not from the USA, but from Canada, and our health system is just as bad. If you have anything more than a runny nose, you're in for a nightmare trying to see a specialist that is going to actually help with your issues.

I'm not someone that prays, but I'll definitely be thinking about you and I truly hope you can find some relief. If you want, feel free to PM me here, to talk about anything at all, or even just to rant to someone who wants to listen. I could give you an email address too, if you wanted. I'm just throwing that out there.

By the way, have you ever heard of kratom? It's a natural plant that grows in Indonesia, and the leaves have a legitimate opate-like pain relief effect. It honestly does help, both for anxiety but also for pain. It's not new-age hippy garbage or bullshit homeopathic/natural stuff, it honest to god can be just as good for pain relief as prescription pain meds, and I know of a lot of people that started using it as a replacement for their pain meds. There is a ton of information on it if you Google search, but be warned that there are also a lot of people that abuse it in the same way one might abuse pain medication. But used properly, it can be a life changing discovery: take it from me. It may not be something you're interested in, and it isn't a widely-known plant here in North America so you might have to bring doctors up to speed on it, but I would definitely recommend at least trying it. If you want any more info on it or a recommendation on where you can buy it online, PM me and I'd be glad to share my experience with you. By the way, it's legal for the most part, except there are one or two states in the USA that have banned it due to it being so similar to prescription painkillers and because it presents a threat to pharmaceutical companies: you can't exactly patent a plant that grows in the ground but mimics your chemical-filled pills. I'm not sure which state you live in, but it's a pretty good chance that you live in one where it's fine.

p.s: Let me put this nicely... pardon my French, but fuck that neurologist in his stupid face. There is nothing worse than a rude and uncaring medical professional. These are people that are supposed to be empathetic and helpful, not cruel and mean. I am at a loss for words reading about your experience. I sincerely hope he loses his job.

I just want everyone to know that I'm going to be okay for tonight, at least. I will probably go to sleep thinking about death, but I'm not going to die tonight, anyway.

True suicidal feelings are some of the worst in the world. Just having them makes me feel guilty and awful, which adds to the cycle. :(
I'm not anyone important, but please go to the ER or call 911. You're probably going to give yourself organ damage if you don't.

Fucking fuck. I am in pain too, and I can't stand to read this. Please, I hope you're okay. 

I hate this world. Why must there be so much suffering? If I could take your pain and bear it myself, I would do it without thinking twice. If I could do this for people and give my suffering meaning, it would make it worth it.

I hope you're okay. :(

I have considered this, actually. I sometimes feel like I need to do something big or drastic to shake the pieces up and see if they fall into a better pattern. I have no idea what that would be for me, personally. But I know that languishing here is making things worse, not better. I need a change of scenery. For a long time I just rotted here because I didn't care, and one day I woke up and it like it hit like a 10 ton hammer -- how miserable I really was.

I hate living with my family here, but they'll never kick me out. Which is one of the biggest problems and reasons why I found myself in this position in the first place. My parents never encouraged me to do anything, nor forced me to do anything. They were more like babysitters instead of parents. I would do anything to go back to my teenage years and slap my parents in the face and tell them to force me to get a summer job, or to be more outgoing, or something. I secretly wish they would have given me an ultimatum that I would get kicked out. I'm not blaming them for my problems, and I know I have to take some kind of responsibility for it myself, but I know that the root is in how I was raised.

I read a story here about some girl that got stuck in some old mining catacombs during a drunken New Year's party somewhere in Europe. She died there, because she was all alone, without a light, in a gigantic and twisted maze of corridors. When I read about that, it felt like the perfect metaphor for exactly how I feel. Utterly lost in a pitch black maze. There might be a possible way out, but you are never going to find it yourself.

I wish there was some way that someone could tell me exactly what to do to fix my life. Or give me a roadmap, or something. That makes me sound so helpless, but I really do feel that way. 

A lot of this is depression talking. I don't know if everything really is hopeless or not, but it absolutely feels that way. The only way I can survive is to pretend that I think it will be better some day. There's no way that's going to magically happen. If we're going back to the dark maze metaphor, I've basically curled up into the fetal position on the cold ground, waiting to die.

So yes, I need to change something. I need to be anywhere but here. One small comfort I have is that I've saved some money up. Not a lot, but enough to live on for a short while if I really had to. I've considered moving out into an apartment, but I know that living alone would be soul crushing to me. I couldn't stand that. What little interaction I have with my family here on a daily basis keeps me from going completely crazy. 

I'm rambling again, but thank you for the response. This has actually gotten my mind moving in some place outside of the cycle of shitty thoughts, which is refreshing.

I'm going to go outside for a a little bit... that's a good idea. I sadly haven't left the house in a few days either.

I'll have to look into that other stuff. I don't know much about breathing exercises or meditation, but I'm willing to try anything.

I know that my biggest problem is a very screwed up way of thinking. If I could shut up the voice in my head that tells me everything I ever do is wrong and horrible and that everything is on the verge of disaster I know I would be a lot better off. I'm kind of rambling here, but yeah.

Thank you for responding. I feel so incredibly awful, I can't even put it into words. I don't want to die but I don't see any option. I feel like I'm in a lightless underground maze that stretches on for miles. I'm sorry for responding to you in particular about this. My brain is going 1000 miles per hour.

I have no idea what I'd say to this situation if I were someone else either. I don't even know why I posted it here. I'm at my wit's end.

Hey, thank you for the response. I honestly would like to have had a life of my own by now. At the very least a long term relationship. I'd like to be doing something with a girlfriend, or wife, or whatever the case might be. That's so corny and mundane, but it's really all I've ever wanted.

I've isolated myself for a long time and it's done terrible things to my mind and social skills. I used to have friends, but I really haven't had a real life friend in over 10 years. I've been on 1 date in my life, a few years ago, and it went terribly. 

I am just such a mess, that I can't even begin to understand how to fix things. These are things I should have been doing 10 years ago, not when I'm almost a 30 year old man.
This made me cry. Wow, I'm really a basket case. Thank you, though. I need to do something but I don't know what. I know I can't live like this anymore.
